brief.subject: IRS final rules clear the way for direct card payments
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Rules Letting It Take Card Tax Payments Directly
brief.dek: Final IRS card-payment rules, a proposed premium tax credit overhaul, Ohio use tax on untaxed wine orders, and retirement distribution reporting.
brief.lede: The IRS has issued final rules under the Taxpayer First Act that let it take credit and debit card tax payments itself, without a third-party processor.

sections.heading: IRS can now take cards directly
bullets: Final regulations let the IRS accept credit and debit card tax payments itself, cutting out the third-party processor step.
The rules carry out Taxpayer First Act changes, so how businesses pay by card could shift.
Restrictions on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts are removed, which could change who bears processing costs.

sections.heading: Premium tax credit rules under review
bullets: The IRS proposed changes to who qualifies for the premium tax credit and how the credit is calculated.
Self-employed owners buying Exchange coverage for themselves or family should watch closely; the rules reach eligibility and credit amounts.
The proposal also covers liability for excess advance credit payments, which can mean a bigger bill at filing time.

sections.heading: Ohio: no tax charged isn't tax-free
bullets: Ohio treats a seller's duty to collect tax separately from a buyer's duty to pay it.
A wine order with no Ohio tax on the receipt can still leave the buyer owing it.
Exemptions and credits can reduce the amount due, so check before assuming nothing is owed.

sections.heading: Retirement distributions must be reported
bullets: The IRS is rejecting claims that IRA and qualified plan recipients didn't know they had to report distributions.
Owners and freelancers drawing on retirement accounts should report every distribution to avoid disputes with the IRS.

brief.seo_description: IRS finalizes direct card payment rules, proposes premium tax credit changes; plus Ohio use tax and retirement distribution reporting for small businesses.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. items.title: Rule: Non-Applicability of Section 357(c) to Consolidated Groups
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations clarifying that, in the case of certain transfers between members of a consolidated group, a transferee's assumption of certain liabilities will not reduce the transferor's basis in the transferee's stock received in the transfer. These final regulations affect consolidated groups and their members.
